newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechnya threatens to shoot down Russian planes.
newsitem.headline: Chechnya threatens to shoot down Russian planes.

text.p: The acting leader of the separatist region of Chechnya threatened on Wednesday to shoot down any Russian aircraft which flies over it, Interfax news agency said.

It quoted Vakha Arsanov, who is standing in for President Aslan Maskhadov who is away on the traditional Moslem piligrimage or haj, as saying in a statement that the threats would take effect from midnight (2000 GMT on Wednesday).
"The Russian air force has been invading the Chechen air space with increasing frequency in recent days," Interfax quoted the statement as saying.

"The (Chechen) republic's armed forces have taken all the necessary steps to protect Chechen air space...The Russian leadership will bear the full weight of responsibility for the consequences of these steps if they have to be taken."

It was not clear whether Arsanov was acting independently or on behalf of the Chechen leadership. It was also not clear whether Maskhadov, with whom Moscow says it can do business, was aware of the proposal and backed it.
Moscow and Chechnya's separatist leaders signed a ceasefire last August after almost 21 months of fighting over the mainly Moslem region's breakaway drive, but Russia has ruled out full independence.
The dispute means Moscow and the separatists both regard the airspace over Chechnya as their own.
Chechnya is awash with weapons but it is not clear how extensive the region's air defences are.
